checks.check: Every page and action that should need sign-in refuses someone signed out
checks.how: List the approved private pages and actions. Check the server's sign-in rules and run the project's normal signed-out tests.
checks.not_applicable: No page or action is supposed to require sign-in.

checks.check: A user sees and changes only their own things (tried with two accounts)
checks.how: Use the project's test with two ordinary sample accounts. Confirm the permitted account can read and change its sample record and the other account is refused.
checks.not_applicable: Users have no account-owned data or actions that must be kept private from other accounts.

checks.check: Admin pages and actions are refused to a non-admin, on the server
checks.how: Check server rules for each admin page and action. Run the normal permission tests for an admin and an ordinary sample account.
checks.not_applicable: No page or action is reserved for an administrator.

checks.check: Passwords are saved scrambled, never as plain text
checks.how: Follow password setup and reset to storage. Check that the app saves a password hash and run its password storage test if it has one.
checks.not_applicable: Password storage belongs entirely to another service, or sign-in uses no passwords.

checks.check: A password reset link stops working after a set time
checks.how: Read the expiry rule and run the project's existing reset test with a sample link and a test clock beyond the limit.
checks.not_applicable: The project neither issues nor requires password reset links.

checks.check: No default account or default password is left
checks.how: Review setup scripts, sample accounts and release settings for an account or password enabled by default.
checks.not_applicable: The project neither uses nor requires sign-in accounts.

checks.check: A session stops working after sign-out
checks.how: Read the sign-out handler and use the project's session test to confirm a signed-out session cannot open a private page.
checks.not_applicable: The project neither uses nor requires sign-in sessions.

checks.check: No password, key or token is written in the code
checks.how: Review the code and tracked settings for saved credential values. Record only the setting name or where it was found.
checks.not_applicable: The project contains no code or tracked settings to review.

checks.check: None is in the git history
checks.how: Review local Git history or a recent redacted history check. Record locations or results without recording any credential value.
checks.not_applicable: The checked copy has no Git folder or Git worktree pointer. If it has one but the history is unavailable, mark fail.

checks.check: Settings come from the environment, and the example settings file holds names only
checks.how: Follow the code that loads settings. Check that it reads from the environment and compare its setting names with the example file. If there is no example file, use the setting names listed in an approved document or the guide as the example.
checks.not_applicable: The project has no runtime or release settings to supply and the approved documents require none.

checks.check: Local settings files are ignored by git
checks.how: Compare the project's local settings files with its Git ignore rules and tracked file list.
checks.not_applicable: The checked copy has no Git folder or Git worktree pointer, or has no local settings files to keep out of Git.

checks.check: The source-control folder cannot be reached from outside
checks.how: Read the release package list and server rules. Check that the source-control folder is excluded or explicitly blocked.
checks.not_applicable: The checked copy has no source-control folder or pointer, or it neither serves nor distributes files from its source tree.

checks.check: Debug mode is off and error details are not shown to users
checks.how: Inspect release settings and error handling. Use an existing ordinary failure test to see what users receive, including in a terminal.
checks.not_applicable: The project has neither a debug mode nor any way to show or return errors to users.

checks.check: Everything a user sends is checked on the server, not only in the browser
checks.how: Trace each user input to its server checks. Run the project's own tests for ordinary invalid or missing values.
checks.not_applicable: The project neither has nor requires a server that accepts user input.

checks.check: Database queries use placeholders
checks.how: Read the database calls and check that user values are bound separately from query text.
checks.not_applicable: The project makes no database queries.

checks.check: Text from users cannot run as code on a page
checks.how: Follow user text to every web page or generated HTML page that shows it. Check that templates escape it or render it as text. Try ordinary text containing punctuation in a local test.
checks.not_applicable: No web page or generated HTML shows text from users, and the approved documents require no such display.

checks.check: File uploads are limited by type and size
checks.how: For this check, count every way the project takes in files, such as a server upload, opening a file with the app or a cable transfer. Read the rules for each way and use sample files to try the accepted types and size limits.
checks.not_applicable: The project neither accepts nor requires file uploads.

checks.check: Prices and totals are worked out on the server
checks.how: Follow an order to the server's calculation and check that it uses its own price list. Run the normal totals test.
checks.not_applicable: The project neither works out nor requires prices or totals on a server.

checks.check: Steps cannot be skipped or done out of order
checks.how: Trace the required order of steps to its state rules. Run an existing test that checks the rule for an unfinished earlier step.
checks.not_applicable: No project action has a required earlier step.

checks.check: The connection is encrypted and plain HTTP is refused or redirected
checks.how: Read the release settings and existing test results for encrypted connections. For an HTTP service, also look for evidence that plain HTTP is refused or redirected.
checks.not_applicable: The project uses no network connections and the approved documents require none.

checks.check: Only the right sites may call the service
checks.how: Compare the service's allowed web origins and access rules with the approved sites. Review the project's existing access tests.
checks.not_applicable: The project has no service for browser calls and requires none.

checks.check: The security headers are set
checks.how: Review response and release settings for the headers the service needs. Use an existing response test or captured headers as proof.
checks.not_applicable: The project neither sends nor requires HTTP responses.

checks.check: Sign-in cookies carry their safe settings
checks.how: Read the sign-in cookie setup and any response test. Check Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite and scope against the way sign-in works.
checks.not_applicable: The project neither uses nor requires browser sign-in cookies.

checks.check: Forms are protected against forgery
checks.how: Read the form and server protections for actions made with browser credentials. Check the existing form tests.
checks.not_applicable: No browser action changes data or settings using credentials the browser sends automatically.

checks.check: Nothing sensitive is in a web address
checks.how: Read routes, links and redirects that carry user data or credentials. Check the shape of the address in an ordinary local test.
checks.not_applicable: The project uses no web addresses in routes, links, redirects or requests.

checks.check: Repeated tries are limited on sign-in and on costly actions
checks.how: Read the attempt limits and tests for sign-in and each costly action. Look for the result when a permitted test limit is reached.
checks.not_applicable: The project has neither sign-in nor a repeatable action with a direct cost or heavy use of limited resources.

checks.check: It saves what the approved Data document says and nothing more
checks.how: Compare the approved saved fields with the files, database records and logs the project writes. Make a normal sample record if a safe local test is available.
checks.not_applicable: The project saves no data and the approved documents require none to be saved.

checks.check: A backup exists
checks.how: Find a dated copy or a record of a successful backup for the required data. A record counts only if it is dated after the last change to the shape of the saved data. A separate paper copy can count if it holds the records needed to recover. Recovery instructions alone do not show that a copy exists.
checks.not_applicable: The project has no data to preserve after loss. An approved recovery route using a separate copy, including a paper copy, makes the check apply.

checks.check: Getting the data back from that backup was tried
checks.how: Find dated evidence that the required data was restored from its backup or approved recovery copy. If needed, try the written restore steps with a sample copy on a disposable local project.
checks.not_applicable: The project has no data to recover after loss. An approved recovery route using a separate copy, including a paper copy, makes the check apply.

checks.check: Database changes are ready to run on the live copy
checks.how: Read the migration files and written release steps. Compare them with a recorded trial on a disposable copy of matching data.
checks.not_applicable: The release requires no database schema or data migration.

checks.check: Personal data is kept and removed as the approved documents say
checks.how: Follow personal fields, such as names and contact details, through storage and removal. Compare those rules and any recorded test with the approved requirements.
checks.not_applicable: The project neither stores personal data nor has an approved rule for keeping or removing personal data. Check non-personal retention under the saved-data check.

checks.check: The copy that will go live is the copy that was tested
checks.how: For each intended target in the approved delivery scope, find a record already kept with the project that ties that copy to a successful test run. Compare the candidate with this record using the channel users will receive. For one file, use the SHA-256 of the final file after packaging and any signing. For a repository delivered as source, use the full commit resolved from a clean checkout through the user's channel. For a copied folder, use the SHA-256 of the retained list of shipped relative paths and file hashes in stable order. Rebuild the list from the delivered bytes using the saved recipe and the same documented exclusions. Changed line endings count as different unless a previously documented text rule applies to both lists. For every other delivery, use the version and full source commit from the running, installed or fetched copy. When distinct builds share those values, include an existing observable build or deployment ID. In the reason, record each target, its actual identity values, the record location and the finding. Mark pass only when every intended target matches its passing record. Mark fail if evidence is missing, stale, inaccessible, mismatched or ambiguous. On fail, identify the affected target and name the record the owner must supply in the reason. A comparison the checker makes during the check is supporting evidence only and cannot make this check pass. In every later round, retry this check and set its round to the current project round.
checks.not_applicable: No deployment or handover of a runnable copy is planned.

checks.check: A way back to the last version exists and was tried
checks.how: Read the recovery steps and look for a dated trial on a safe copy with the intended previous version.
checks.not_applicable: This is the first release, with no earlier live version to restore.

checks.check: The packages it uses have no known serious weakness
checks.how: List the installed or locked package versions. Compare them with a dated dependency report or advisory data already available in the project.
checks.not_applicable: The project uses no third-party packages.

checks.check: Every action works from the keyboard and focus is never trapped
checks.how: Try the main tasks and each control with a keyboard in the local interface. Open and close each dialog and check where focus goes. For a terminal tool, run the commands and try any interactive prompts.
checks.not_applicable: The project has no user-operated interface.

checks.check: Text has readable contrast
checks.how: Check each foreground and background pair the tool sets, including optional modes and errors. Plain output that sets neither colour inherits the host pair and needs no project colour measurement. If the tool sets only one colour, check it against the other colour on each approved host theme. Mark pass when all pairs the tool controls are shown readable.
checks.not_applicable: The project displays no text to a person.

checks.check: Pictures that carry meaning have a text alternative
checks.how: Review each picture with meaning and inspect its text alternative in the interface or source.
checks.not_applicable: The project has no pictures or icons needed to understand or use it.

checks.check: Fields have labels and errors say which field
checks.how: Inspect the label or name for each input, including prompts and command arguments. Omit or mistype an ordinary value in a local test and read the error.
checks.not_applicable: The user enters no values through fields, prompts or command arguments.

checks.check: Every page has a title and its language set
checks.how: Inspect each page's title and language metadata in the local app or its templates.
checks.not_applicable: The project presents no web pages or generated HTML pages.

checks.check: A new user finishes the main task the first time, using only what is on the screen
checks.how: Use a trial with a person unfamiliar with the project. Watch them try the main task using what the interface shows, or read a record of that trial on the same interface. For a terminal tool, include its built-in help.
checks.not_applicable: The project gives an end user no task to do. A task carried out in the terminal makes the check apply.

checks.check: The words are plain and the same thing has the same name everywhere
checks.how: Read the main screens, instructions and errors. Compare the names for the same actions and objects across them.
checks.not_applicable: The project has no words for users in its interface, output, errors or instructions.

checks.check: A user can see where they are and can go back
checks.how: Walk each user flow. Check that the current step or screen is clear and try the available way back.
checks.not_applicable: The project has no flow that takes a user through more than one screen or prompt. Separate one-step terminal commands are not a multi-step flow.

checks.check: An error message says what went wrong and what to do
checks.how: Try a normal, safe error in a local test and read the message. Review the source for other errors users can see.
checks.not_applicable: There is no user action that can fail or reject input.

checks.check: It works on the devices the approved documents name
checks.how: Use the named devices or read test evidence from those devices for the main tasks.
checks.not_applicable: The approved documents name no device or class of devices.

checks.check: It meets the speed the approved documents name
checks.how: Run the local timing test under the stated conditions or compare a recorded result with the approved target.
checks.not_applicable: The approved documents name no speed target.

checks.check: The main database queries are fast
checks.how: Review local timings or query plans on sample data of a useful size. Compare them with the project's performance evidence.
checks.not_applicable: The project makes no database queries.

checks.check: It was tried under load before launch
checks.how: Find a dated test record for realistic demand. If needed, run the project's bounded load test on a disposable local copy.
checks.not_applicable: The planned use is one operation at a time, with no batch work or higher demand to reproduce.

checks.check: Following the written guide, someone who did not build it can start it on an empty computer
checks.how: Have a person who did not build the project follow only the written guide on a clean test computer, or read a record of that trial.
checks.not_applicable: Nobody other than the builder is expected to start the project.

checks.check: Errors are recorded, with no password or key in the record
checks.how: Try an ordinary error on a safe copy or read its existing test record. Check what the project records and how it leaves out credentials.
checks.not_applicable: The project runs no operations that could fail during use. It also does not apply if one person is the only user, sees every error on screen, and no approved document requires an error record.

checks.check: Someone is told when it fails, and a named person owns that
checks.how: Use the approved failure instructions to find the owner and notification route. A manual handoff counts for an attended tool when a dated trial shows the named recipient was told. For unattended work, require a trial of the configured alert. A named route without a trial is fail.
checks.not_applicable: The project has no unattended service or background work and the approved documents name no duty to tell someone about a software failure. Instructions for a lost device or a leak alone do not count as a duty to tell for this check.

checks.check: Users have a way to report a problem
checks.how: Find the contact or reporting path in the app or guide and confirm it is listed without sending a message.
checks.not_applicable: The project has no users or operators other than the builder. It also does not apply when the owner is the only user, even if the owner builds through AI agents.

checks.check: Everything the approved Handover names exists
checks.how: Find each item promised in the approved Handover and check that it opens or can be used.
checks.not_applicable: There is no approved Handover or it promises no items.
